questions.text: How did the Subsidiary Alliance system help in the expansion of the British Empire?

answer.value:
The British forced Indian rulers to adopt this system.
Indian rulers had to maintain a British army in their court and bear its entire cost.
Alternatively, they had to cede a part of their territory to the British.
Thus, many Indian kingdoms came under British control.

questions.text: What were the causes of the Battle of Buxar?
questions.text_as_printed: What were the causes of the Battle of Buxar? (Difficult )

answer.value:
Causes of the Battle of Buxar:
The Nawab of Bengal, Mir Qasim, was independent-minded.
He scrutinized the dastaks (trade permits) being misused by the British.
The British, enraged by this, deposed Mir Qasim.
The enraged Mir Qasim formed a military alliance and attacked the British.

questions.text: How did the Battle of Buxar help the British establish their supremacy in India? Explain.
questions.text_as_printed: How did the Battle of Buxar help the British establish their supremacy in India? Explain. (Average )

answer.value: After their victory at Buxar the British became more powerful and the weakened Mughal king sought refuge with them. This paved the way for the Grant of Diwani Rights in 1765: Robert Clive entered into a treaty with the Mughal ruler Shah Alam II, under which the Company paid 26 lakh rupees a year and obtained the Diwani (the right to collect land revenue) of Bengal (including Assam), Bihar and Odisha. Through this Diwani right the East India Company acquired official sovereignty in Bengal and freedom to levy and collect taxes, making the Company the real ruling power in India.

questions.text: Why was the Doctrine of Lapse considered unjustified?
questions.text_as_printed: Why was the Doctrine of Lapse considered unjustified? (Difficult )

answer.value:
The Doctrine of Lapse introduced by Lord Dalhousie was completely against the long-established Indian custom of adopting children.
It declared that the adopted son of a childless Indian ruler had no right to inherit the throne, thereby depriving rulers of their natural right.
This policy was implemented solely to expand British power and wealth, without serving any public interest, and it hurt the religious and social beliefs of the Indian people.

questions.text: How did the British take control of power in India through the Regulating Act?
questions.text_as_printed: How did the British take control of power in India through the Regulating Act? (Difficult)

answer.value: The British Parliament passed the Regulating Act in 1773 to properly regulate and control the activities of the East India Company, whose officials had been extorting money through unscrupulous means. Under the Act, Warren Hastings was appointed the first Governor General. During this period the British converted Calcutta into their centre of power and took control of the activities of the provincial governments. (The defects of the Regulating Act were later corrected by the Pitt's India Act of 1784.)

questions.text: Explain how British power gradually increased in South India.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain how British power gradually increased in South India. (Average )

answer.value:
The British government checked the unethical ways of the Company officials through the Regulating Act introduced by Warren Hastings.
The British made Calcutta their center of power and brought the functioning of the provincial government under their control.
Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan fought against the British.
The Mysore kingdom was divided into four parts: one part went to the British, one to the Nizam, another to the Marathas, and the remaining part to the Mysore ruler.
This led to a gradual increase in British power in India.
